who: William L. Barney, historian of nineteenth-century America and the Civil War at UNC Chapel Hill from 1975; PhD in U.S. history, Columbia, 1971.

evidence.says: The UNC History chair's professional tribute identifies William L. Barney, Columbia PhD in U.S. history in 1971, on the UNC faculty from 1975; it lists Road to Secession, Flawed Victory and Battleground for the Union.
The candidate's LC authority identifies William L. Barney through The Road to Secession and The Secessionist Impulse, and also names Battleground for the Union and Flawed Victory.

notes: Exact doctorate and institution match; the shared publications establish the LC identity.

who: Josef J. Barton, Northwestern historian of U.S. immigration and labor and Latin America; PhD Michigan, 1971.

evidence.says: Northwestern gives Josef Barton's PhD as Michigan, 1971, and identifies him as the author of Peasants and Strangers (1975).
The 2008-09 Northwestern catalogue lists Josef Barton, PhD Michigan, as an associate professor of history.
The authority for Barton, Josef J. (Josef John), cites Peasants and Strangers (1975), whose title page names Josef J. Barton.

notes: Doctorate, university during the students' period, and the authority's book all agree.

who: Katherine Benton-Cohen, Georgetown historian of U.S. immigration, gender and the American West; PhD Wisconsin-Madison, 2002.

evidence.says: Georgetown identifies its history professor Katherine Benton-Cohen as the author of Borderline Americans (2009), with a Wisconsin doctorate.
The October 22, 2018 announcement's prose says Benton-Cohen received her history PhD there in 2002 and was a Georgetown associate professor.
Georgetown's December 2018 article says Benton-Cohen arrived at Georgetown in 2007.
The candidate's authority identifies Katherine Benton-Cohen through Borderline Americans (2009).

notes: The degree, Georgetown career and shared book match. Wisconsin's announcement heading says 2012, but its prose says 2002, agreeing with AHA.

who: Judith A. Allen, Indiana University historian of gender, sexuality and crime; PhD Macquarie, 1985.

evidence.says: Indiana's history profile lists Judith Allen as Distinguished Professor and Walter Professor, gives a Macquarie PhD in 1985, and lists Sex and Secrets (1990).
The department's January 2016 news names Judith Allen as the recipient of a 2016-17 Kinsey Institute fellowship for research on Kinsey.
The candidate's LC authority identifies Judith A. Allen through Sex & Secrets (1990).

notes: Indiana affiliation in the students' period and the matching book connect the supervisor to the authority.

who: Engseng Ho, Duke professor of cultural anthropology studying Indian Ocean diasporas; PhD anthropology, Chicago, 2000.

evidence.says: Duke lists Ho's professorship from 2008, his Chicago anthropology doctorate in 2000, and his book The Graves of Tarim.
Duke names Engseng Ho as advisor for Janice Hyeju Jeong's 2019 history dissertation Between Shanghai and Mecca.
The authority for Ho, Engseng, cites The Graves of Tarim (2006).

notes: Direct student-advisor confirmation and the shared book establish the match, despite Ho's departmental appointment in anthropology.

who: Peter Wien, University of Maryland historian of the modern Middle East; PhD Bonn, 2003.

evidence.says: Maryland identifies Peter Wien as professor of modern Middle Eastern history, with a Bonn PhD in 2003 and a former fellowship at the Centre for Modern Oriental Studies in Berlin.
The repository record for Alda Benjamen's 2015 Maryland history dissertation lists Wien, Peter, as advisor.
The candidate's authority cites Blind für die Geschichte? (2004), identifying Peter Wien with Zentrum Moderner Orient, Berlin.

notes: Direct advisor confirmation, Bonn doctorate and the authority's Berlin affiliation agree.

who: Frank Schumacher, Western University historian of U.S. international history and empire; Dr. phil. Cologne, 1997.

The researcher profile identifies Frank Schumacher at Western's History Department and lists Archives in Germany (2001) among his edited volumes.
The candidate's authority identifies Frank Schumacher through Archives in Germany (2001).
Oliver Charbonneau's Civilizational Imperatives acknowledgments say the project began with Schumacher in 2010 and describe his guidance, alongside other Western history faculty.

notes: Cologne doctorate, Western affiliation and the shared edited volume establish the candidate's identity.

who: Hayes Baker-Crothers, University of Maryland history professor from 1925; PhD Wisconsin, 1924, and coauthor of Problems of Citizenship.

evidence.says: Martha Jackson Ross's departmental history identifies Hayes Baker-Crothers as Maryland's first history professor with a history PhD, arriving in 1925.
The departmental history, page 18, gives his Wisconsin PhD in 1924.
The 1926 publisher advertisement for Problems of Citizenship names Hayes Baker-Crothers, University of Maryland, as coauthor.
The authority for Baker-Crothers, Hayes, cites Problems of Citizenship (1924) and records the alternate form Crothers, Hayes Baker.

notes: The authority's book is explicitly attributed to the Maryland professor in a contemporary publisher advertisement.
